compile_command: clang -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror Sources/SearchCore/SearchCore.c Sources/SearchCore/SearchQuery.c Sources/SearchCore/SearchTokenizer.c Tests/SearchCoreTests.c -I Sources/SearchCore -lsqlite3 -framework CoreFoundation -o /tmp/argus-core-tests

fulltext_search.text: Repeated English sentence; tests first-indexed-match excerpts on common terms.

metadata_only_search.scope: Name prefixes, exact/substrings, metadata/pinyin aliases; excludes fuzzy and body stages.

correctness_checks: Empty and singleton queries; literal punctuation; SQL injection input; invalid UTF-8; term limit
Case, accents, full-width normalization; Chinese one-character and substring matches; pinyin aliases
Transposed and first-letter typos; spaced initial subsequences; multiple keywords and path terms
File/folder/application filters; exact-name priority; NUL-terminated UTF-8 buffers
Content timestamp persistence; changed-file invalidation; empty extraction; 32 KiB UTF-8 cap
Chinese gram false-positive rejection; late diacritic and Chinese excerpt byte offsets
Separate WAL handles: uncommitted rows hidden, committed rows visible, rollback preserved
Cross-thread sqlite interruption observed; subsequent reader query succeeds
Directory-prefix boundaries; streaming exclusion predicate; 100k-row missing-file prune
Text clearing, content-byte counter, FTS compaction, VACUUM and WAL truncation
Metadata-only API shares validation and cancellation recovery; body-only and typo-only hits arrive only in full search.
limitations: Timings are this synthetic workload on warm local storage, not a guaranteed bound for every query or dataset.
Candidate caps trade exhaustive recall for bounded work on very broad and fuzzy queries.
Fulltext returns tied body matches in candidate order and stops when requested result capacity is filled.
CJK fulltext candidates are checked for contiguous normalized keywords; more than 512 false-positive gram candidates can hide later valid rows.
Pinyin aliases are supplied for metadata; bodies are not transliterated.
Single-character non-CJK metadata queries scan rows; rare characters can cost more than indexed multi-character queries.
The caller enforces the global extracted-text budget and filesystem scope.
App memory footprint and cold-cache searches were not measured by this C harness.
